q: Neha opens a new AI chat to start planning her LinkedIn content. What is the most effective first step, according to the course workflow?
options: Ask the AI to write ten viral posts about her industry right away
Ask the AI to interview her with questions about her experience and audience
Ask the AI to pick the opinions she should hold on industry topics
Ask the AI to copy the style of the top creators in her niche
explain: The "interview me first" approach makes the AI collect your raw material before writing, so suggestions are specific to you rather than generic.

q: Rahul writes formally but speaks naturally. What is the best voice sample to add when building his brand voice guide?
options: A transcript of him explaining his work aloud for a few minutes
His most formal annual report summary from last year
A competitor's popular posts that he admires
An AI-written sample post about his job title
explain: Spoken samples often capture a person's natural voice better than stiff writing, so a transcript is a strong sample.

q: After AI describes Sana's likely core reader based on five client questions, what should she do next?
options: Accept the description, since AI has analysed the market for her
Treat it as a hypothesis and check it by talking to a few real people
Widen the description so the content appeals to a larger audience
Ask a second AI tool and keep whichever description sounds better
explain: AI audience descriptions are guesses, so the course says to verify them with two or three people who fit the description.

q: Vikram wants to plan his 30-day content calendar. What should he decide first?
options: How much time he realistically has each week and which platforms matter most
Which festivals he can post greetings for during the month
How to post every day on four platforms to grow faster
Which hashtags are trending this month in his industry
explain: The course says to start with capacity, not ambition, because consistency beats volume.

q: Why does the course's calendar prompt include a column called "raw material I need to supply"?
options: To list the design assets the AI tool will generate automatically
To track which posts have been approved by a manager
To remind you each post needs something only you can provide, like a story or real number
To record which AI tool was used for each post
explain: The column ensures every post contains your own stories, photos or data rather than generic AI content.

q: When drafting a LinkedIn post from her notes, which instruction best stops the AI from inventing statistics?
options: Do not add any facts, numbers or claims that are not in my notes
Make the post sound as convincing and data-driven as possible
Include at least three statistics to support the main point
Write it in the style of a well-known business influencer
explain: Explicitly forbidding facts not in the notes prevents the AI from making up numbers to sound persuasive.

q: Priya has an 8-step onboarding checklist she gives clients. Which LinkedIn format suits it best?
options: A single short opinion post with no structure
A celebration post announcing a recent win
A carousel with one idea per slide that people can save
A poll asking followers which step they skip
explain: Carousels work best for processes, checklists and frameworks with a natural sequence that people want to save.

q: Karan wants to know which of three hooks works best for the same reel. What does the course recommend?
options: Pick the hook the AI rated highest and use only that one
Use all three hooks back to back at the start of one video
Ask followers in a poll which hook they prefer before filming
Record the body once with three hooks and compare early retention
explain: Testing variants with the same body and comparing retention past the first seconds shows which hook works.

q: An AI draft starts "In today's fast-paced world" and ends "Agree? Share below!" What is the first edit pass?
options: Run it through an AI detector until it scores as human
Add more emojis and hashtags to make it feel casual
Ask the AI to make it sound more inspirational
Delete the generic opening and the engagement-bait closing line
explain: Pass 1 of the five-pass edit removes throat-clearing openers and generic engagement bait.

q: Anil wants to write a long-form article with AI that reflects his expertise. What is the recommended starting point?
options: Ask the AI to write the full 1,500-word article in one go
Choose a broad topic and let the AI pick the angle
Pick a specific audience question and have the AI interview him
Paste a competitor's article and ask for a rewrite
explain: Starting from a specific question and a self-interview makes the article built on his own expertise.

q: Before writing an article targeting a keyword, why should you search it and look at the top results?
options: To copy the structure and wording of the top-ranking page
To understand the search intent and the format searchers expect
To count how many times competitors repeat the keyword
To find backlinks you can buy from those websites
explain: The top results show what searchers want, such as lists, guides or videos, which guides your format.

q: A creator turns one newsletter into ten pieces. What is the right first step with AI?
options: Paste the same newsletter text on every platform the same day
Ask AI to write ten new unrelated posts on the same topic
Extract the distinct ideas, stories and lines as atoms, then map them to formats
Turn the newsletter into a single long video and stop there
explain: Extracting idea atoms first lets you map each one to the format and platform that suits it.

q: Meena is not fluent in Tamil but wants to post a Tamil caption written by AI. What is the safest approach?
options: Ask for a back-translation and have a fluent person review before posting
Ask for formal literary Tamil since it is always more correct
Post it directly, since AI handles all Indian languages accurately
Translate it word-for-word from English to keep the meaning exact
explain: Back-translation helps catch meaning errors, but only publish in a language you or a trusted reviewer can check fluently.

q: A Pune bakery wants an image for a post about its new cake. Which choice follows the course guidance?
options: Generate a realistic AI cake and post it as their product
Use a stock photo of a similar cake without labelling it
Ask AI to recreate a famous bakery's cake photo
Use a real photo of the actual cake they sell
explain: Products must be shown with real photos; an AI-generated cake presented as theirs misleads customers.

q: A social media manager wants to clone a client doctor's voice for Hindi videos. What is required first?
options: A quick WhatsApp "ok" from the doctor's assistant
Explicit written consent stating the use, platforms, duration and withdrawal
Nothing, as long as the videos are educational
A disclaimer at the end of each video only
explain: Voice cloning needs explicit, informed, written consent for a specific use; a casual message is not enough.

q: Ravi gets free products from a brand and makes a reel about them. How should he disclose this under ASCI guidance?
options: Add #ad at the end of a long list of hashtags in the caption
No disclosure is needed because he was not paid in cash
Mention it only if a follower asks in the comments
Use a clear label like "Ad" upfront and show it in the video itself
explain: Any material connection, including free products, must be disclosed prominently, and in videos the label should appear in the video.

q: Ishaan's goal is winning consulting clients. Which metric should he prioritise?
options: Total likes on each post
Follower count growth from any audience
Number of posts published per week
Enquiries, DMs about his work and calls booked
explain: Metrics should match the goal; for client work, enquiries and booked calls matter more than likes.

q: A consultant with a skill people already pay for asks which monetisation path to start with. What does the course suggest?
options: Platform revenue-sharing programmes
Services, since content proves expertise and services convert that trust
Brand sponsorships, regardless of audience size
A large cohort course before testing demand
explain: If you already have a paid skill, services are usually the fastest and most reliable path.
